planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Ollioules is a mid-season Darwin Hybrid tulip prized for its large, clear rose-pink blooms.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Ollioules produces large, egg-shaped blooms in a clear rose-pink with a paler blush edge and a soft yellow base, held on sturdy, tall stems typical of the Darwin Hybrid class. Its strong stems resist wind and rain better than many other tulip classes, making it a reliable choice for borders and cutting gardens, and it flowers in mid-spring, slightly after the earliest Darwin Hybrids like Apeldoorn. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from wind; Rococo is one of the oldest Parrot tulip cultivars, introduced in the 1940s.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from strong wind and heavy rain. Rococo bears rich scarlet-red petals with green flashes at the base, heavily waved and fringed along the edges in the exaggerated, twisted form typical of Parrot tulips, opening wide as the flower matures. Its shorter, sturdier stems compared to many parrot types make it somewhat less prone to flopping, and it blooms in mid-to-late spring. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Ballade is a late-season Lily-flowered tulip with elegant, pointed, reflexed petals.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Ballade carries slender, pointed petals in vivid magenta-pink edged in white, opening from a narrow goblet into a graceful, star-shaped flower with sharply reflexed tips characteristic of the Lily-flowered class. Its tall, wiry stems and refined silhouette make it a favorite for cutting and for adding vertical elegance to late-spring borders. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: West Point Tulip (Golden Yellow Lily-Flowered Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; West Point is a classic mid-to-late-season Lily-flowered tulip with narrow, twisting golden petals.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. West Point produces narrow, pointed golden-yellow petals that twist gracefully and flare outward as the flower opens, giving it a spidery, star-like silhouette distinctive of the Lily-flowered class. Its slender stems and bright, clean color make it a long-time favorite for formal beds, mixed borders, and cut-flower arrangements, blooming in mid-to-late spring. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Curly Sue Tulip (Wine-Purple Crystalline Fringed Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Curly Sue is a novelty Fringed tulip with deep wine-purple petals edged in fine crystalline fringe.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from strong wind and heavy rain. Curly Sue bears deep wine-purple petals rimmed with a fine, crystalline fringe that catches the light, a delicate texture typical of the Fringed tulip class. Its compact stature and richly colored, ruffled blooms make it well suited to containers and close-up border plantings, flowering in mid-to-late spring. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.
